info.name: 02 - QualityLab E-commerce
info.description:
Product listing and details, admin product management and inventory, cart, checkout and orders.

The admin tests work on a throwaway product created by "Create a product", so real stock is never changed.
The cart is emptied first and the test order is cancelled at the end.
Do not run this at the same time as the Selenium or Playwright suites: they use the same customer's cart.

exec: * DYNAMIC TOKEN HANDLING (runs before every request in this collection)
* A request that needs a session sends the header
* where <module> is ecommerce, banking, travel or admin. Each sign-in opens one module, so
* there is one token per module.
* This script looks at that header. If the token for that module is missing, or expires within
* a minute, it signs in first with pm.sendRequest, using the credentials from the environment
* (testUsername/testPassword, or adminUsername/adminPassword for admin), and saves the token
* and its expiry time as collection variables. Postman waits for the sign-in to finish before
* Why tokens can stop working, and how this script copes:
* The app also sets a session cookie at every sign-in, and a sign-in that sends an older session's
* cookie ends that older session (one browser, one session). Requests here have Settings >
* "Disable cookie jar" on, but pm.sendRequest still uses the cookie jar. So:
*  - after each automatic sign-in the script tries to clear that cookie (Postman needs the API
*    domain on Cookies > Domains Allowlist for this; Newman does not);
*  - when it signs in to a different module, it forgets the previous automatic sign-in's token,
*    in case that sign-in ended it, so the next request for that module signs in again;
*  - the collection's Post-response script forgets any module token the API refuses with 401.
`Set ${admin ? 'adminUsername and adminPassword' : 'testUsername and testPassword'} in the selected environment (Current value).`,
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email, password, module }) },
throw new Error(`Automatic sign-in to ${module} failed: ${error ? error.message : `${response.code} ${response.text()}`}`);
// This sign-in may have sent the previous automatic sign-in's cookie and so ended that
// session. Forget that token; the next request that needs it signs in again.
// Best effort: remove the session cookie this sign-in received, so it is not sent later.
'Tip: add the API domain (for example quality-lab-jb.vercel.app) to Cookies > Domains Allowlist ' +
'to save a few extra sign-ins. The tests work without it.',
* CHECKS FOR EVERY RESPONSE (run after every request in this collection)
* Each request's own Tests tab adds the checks for that request.
pm.test('[every response] no server error (status below 500)', () => {
pm.test('[every response] carries an x-request-id header', () => {
// Every error uses the same shape: { error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }.
pm.test('[every response] error body matches the ErrorResponse schema', () => {
// A module token the API refused (401) is forgotten, so the next request signs in again.
console.warn(`The ${module} token was refused; the next request will sign in again.`);
// A sign-in request in this collection may have sent the last automatic session's cookie and ended
// it, so that token is forgotten too.
